messages.subject: getting wallace to run again
messages.body_plain:
Hi!
Wallace is awesome - compared to my first steps learning maxent and all R data preparations "by foot", six years ago.
I had a few tries, and now I wonder: once Wallace shuts down/gets stuck in the browser - do I have a chance to get it running again - without starting the whole function again?
Thanks for a hint!
Jana

messages.subject: Re: getting wallace to run again
messages.body_plain:
Jana,

Glad you find Wallace so useful! Working in R by foot must take a long time, and probably makes putting on shoes painful...

Sorry that Wallace was shutting down. If Wallace was crashing, could you please post the error message you get so I can try and fix the problem? Also please make sure you’re using v1.0.4, the latest version.

If Wallace does crash and goes gray, the only thing you can do, unfortunately, is start it back up. We are working on ways to start the session from a metadata file, and there may be ways in the future to save a state and load it later, but these features aren’t available currently.

Anyway, please post error messages if you get them (they will appear in the R console).

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of NY

messages.body_plain:
Hey Jamie!

Thank you and everyone else on the Wallace team - this project is awesome. I wanted to share a short and rudimentary tutorial that I wrote https://boyanangelov.com/post/wallace_tutorial/ . I hope you excuse any inaccuracies in my interpretations :) I also plan to create a youtube version and show a demo at our local Berlin R users group - I would like to contribute at least a bit to making this software popular! Let me know what you think.

Have a great day,
- Boyan

messages.subject: Rbind error --> solved (space is species name)
messages.subject_clean: Rbind error --> solved (space is species name)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wallace users,

I encountered the following error when running Wallace (Maxent):

Warning in rbind(train.val, bg.val) :
  number of columns of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 1)
Warning: Error in rep: invalid 'times' argument

We figured out that it is important to leave a space between the genus name and the species name when uploading the occurrence data.
For example, don't use "Homo_sapiens" but make sure it is "Homo sapiens". Even though the software will upload and map data with underscores instead of spaces in species names, it will not run the actual model.

Many thanks to Dr. Jamie Kass for helping with this issue!

King regards,
Hanne
